name: Paracetamol
uses: Used for relieving mild to moderate pain, such as headache, toothache, or muscle aches, and reducing fever.
side_effects: Rarely, allergic reactions such as skin rash or swelling. Long-term use may affect liver function.
how_to_use: Take with water after meals. Do not exceed 4g (8 tablets of 500mg) in 24 hours.
safety_advice: Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine. Consult a doctor if symptoms persist for more than 3 days.

name: Amoxicillin
uses: An antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections like pneumonia, bronchitis, and infections of the ears, nose, throat, urinary tract, and skin.
side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or a skin rash.
how_to_use: Usually taken every 8 or 12 hours with or without food. Complete the full course as prescribed.
safety_advice: Do not use if allergic to penicillin. Inform your doctor about your kidney history.

name: Cetirizine
uses: An antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms and common cold symptoms like watery eyes, runny nose, and sneezing.
how_to_use: Can be taken with or without food, usually once daily.
safety_advice: Be cautious while driving or operating machinery as it may cause drowsiness. Avoid alcohol.

name: Vicks Action 500
uses: Relief from common cold symptoms, nasal congestion, headache, and sore throat.
how_to_use: Take one tablet every 4-6 hours. Do not exceed 4 tablets in 24 hours.
safety_advice: Do not take with other products containing paracetamol.

name: Ibuprofen
uses: Used to relieve pain from various conditions such as headache, dental pain, menstrual cramps, muscle aches, or arthritis. It is also used to reduce fever.
side_effects: Stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, headache, diarrhea, constipation, dizziness, or drowsiness.
how_to_use: Take with food or milk to prevent stomach upset. Usually taken every 4 to 6 hours.
safety_advice: Consult a doctor if you have a history of stomach ulcers or kidney disease. Do not take with other NSAIDs.

name: Loperamide
uses: Used to treat sudden diarrhea (including traveler's diarrhea). It works by slowing down the movement of the gut.
how_to_use: Usually taken after each loose bowel movement. Do not exceed the maximum dose recommended.
safety_advice: Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration. Not for use in children under 2 years old.

name: Omeprazole
uses: Used to treat certain stomach and esophagus problems (such as acid reflux, ulcers). It works by decreasing the amount of acid your stomach makes.
side_effects: Headache or abdominal pain. Long-term use may lead to vitamin B-12 deficiency.
how_to_use: Usually taken once daily, at least 30-60 minutes before a meal.
safety_advice: Inform your doctor if you have liver disease or lupus.

name: Dextromethorphan
uses: A cough suppressant used to temporarily relieve a cough without phlegm (dry cough) caused by air passages irritation (e.g., common cold, flu).
side_effects: Dizziness, lightheadedness, drowsiness, nervousness, restlessness, nausea, or stomach pain.
how_to_use: Take as directed on the label or by your doctor. Usually every 4 to 12 hours.
safety_advice: Do not use if you are taking or have taken an MAO inhibitor in the last 14 days.

name: Guaifenesin
uses: An expectorant used to help clear mucus or phlegm from the chest due to colds, flu, or hay fever.
side_effects: Nausea or vomiting. Stomach pain or dizziness.
how_to_use: Take with a full glass of water to help thin the mucus.
safety_advice: Consult a doctor if cough lasts more than 7 days or occurs with fever or rash.

name: Ranitidine
uses: Used to treat and prevent ulcers in the stomach and intestines. It also treats conditions in which the stomach produces too much acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.
how_to_use: Usually taken once or twice daily, with or without food.
safety_advice: Consult a doctor if symptoms do not improve after 2 weeks of use.
